articles.title: Ethereum remains under pressure amid intensifying geopolitical and macro risks. What's next?
articles.description: Ethereum's fundamental outlook remains mixed, with protocol development and institutional accumulation providing support, while the macro environment remains a headwind. US spot Ethereum ETFs have recently recorded substantial outflows amid deteriorating risk sentiment. In the near term, the geopolitical and macroeconomic picture are likely to matter more for price action than Ethereum’s protocol upgrade alone. Rising oil prices, persistent inflation concerns, higher Treasury yields and hawkish Fed expectations continue to put pressure on the crypto market, so traders will need to see some easing in those concerns to start positioning for new highs. The negotiations between the US and Iran remain at a stalemate, and the Houthis are intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia, raising supply disruption risks and supporting oil prices. Today, the focus will be on the US CPI report. Traders will mainly look at the core m/m measure as Fed members have been focusing on the monthly pace of core inflation to determine how many rate hikes will be needed and how quickly they should tighten policy. An uptick to 0.3% might not be enough for the market to fully expect a hike in October, but a jump to 0.4% should do it. In such a case, we will likely see a selloff in Ethereum on a hawkish repricing. An in-line or even lower than expected figure, on the other hand, could lead to a short-term relief rally for the cryptocurrency. ETHEREUM TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME On the daily chart, we can see that Ethereumis trading near the key support zone around the 2,360 level and the major trendline. We can expect the dip-buyers to step in around the support and the trendline, with a defined risk below the trendline, to position for a rally into the 3,400 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will need the price to break below the trendline to open the door for new lows and target the 1,900 level next. ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 4 hour chart, we can see that the break below the minor upward trendline led to a selloff as more sellers piled in on the break to target the 2,360 support. We have also a downward trendline around the 2,600 level that could act as resistance. If the price gets there, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to position for a drop into the support and the major upward trendline. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 3,400 level next. ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME On the 1 hour chart, we can see the price is consolidating inside a tight box between the 2,485 and 2,535 levels. A break on either side will likely increase the momentum and extend the moves. From a risk management perspective, though, it would be better to wait for the US CPI release as we could see big moves in case of surprises. The red lines define the average daily range for today. UPCOMING CATALYSTS Today we have the US CPI report. Tomorrow, we get the US PPI, the US Retail Sales and the latest US Jobless Claims figures. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Iyer attains career-best fourth spot in T20I rankings after maiden T20I ton
articles.description: India captain Shreyas Iyer has reached a career-high fourth position in the latest ICC T20I rankings for batters after moving up three places following his impressive start to the five-match home series against the West Indies. Iyer smashed his maiden T20I century in the series opener in Lucknow, earning a significant rise in the latest rankings. His ascent to fourth place means India now have three players inside the top four, with Ishan Kishan leading the list and Abhishek Sharma occupying second position. Pakistan captain Sahibzada Farhan sits third after achieving a career-best rating following an impressive performance against Sri Lanka. Other batters making progress in the T20I rankings include Sri Lankaâ€™s Kusal Mendis, who climbed three places to 23rd, West Indiesâ€™ Sherfane Rutherford, who rose 13 spots to share 24th position, and Indiaâ€™s Sanju Samson, who moved up four places to equal 27th. Pakistan youngster Maaz Sadaqat also made a significant jump, rising from outside the top 100 to 45th following his performances in the three-match series against Sri Lanka. In the bowling chart, the West Indies player Roston Chase climbed 24 places to 23rd following his performances against India. He also gained two spots to reach third in the T20I all-roundersâ€™ rankings. Pakistan's Salman Mirza rose nine places to 14th in the T20I bowling rankings, while teammate Saim Ayub climbed eight spots to 54th. There was also significant movement in the Test rankings following Australiaâ€™s 214-run victory over South Africa in the opening match of their three-Test series at Kingsmead in Durban. Australia batter Matthew Renshaw was rewarded for his player of the match performance, which included 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second. The left-hander climbed from outside the top 100 to equal 49th in the Test batting rankings. Former world No. 1 Marnus Labuschagne also moved up four places to 34th, while South Africa opener Aiden Markram climbed four spots to equal 10th. Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood rose two places to seventh in the Test bowling rankings after taking career-best figures of six for 49 on the final day. Teammate Mitchell Starc continued to lead the list, although his advantage over New Zealand pacer Matt Henry narrowed to four rating points. South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje returned to the Test bowling rankings at 34th after playing his first red-ball match in more than three years. Indiaâ€™s Ravindra Jadeja continued to lead the Test all-roundersâ€™ rankings, while South Africaâ€™s Wiaan Mulder climbed one place to fourth and Simon Harmer rose five spots to equal 23rd. Following the drawn one-off test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh in Abu Dhabi, Rahmat Shah climbed 13 places to 13th, and Litton Das moved up three spots to equal 29th in the test batting rankings. While Bangladesh pacer Hasan Mahmud, who took a hat-trick and five wickets in the match, rose seven places to 38th in the bowling rankings.
